title: Practical Quantum Topological Data Analysis with Applications to High-Dimensional Feature Extraction and Time Series Analysis
headline: Quantum Topological Data Analysis Accelerates High-Dimensional Feature Extraction and Time Series Insights
tldr: This work presents a practical quantum algorithm for computing topological invariants efficiently, enabling high-dimensional feature extraction and real-time time series analysis. The authors demonstrate its effectiveness on synthetic and real datasets, highlighting significant speedups over classical methods.
significance: By reducing the computational bottleneck of TDA, this approach opens new possibilities for real-time analysis of complex, high-dimensional data streams.

title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM
headline: TurboVLA: 32 Hz Real-Time Vision-Language-Action on RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM for Deployment
tldr: TurboVLA introduces a lightweight vision-language-action framework that runs at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 while using less than 1 GB of VRAM. By decoupling visual encoding from language decoding, it reduces computational overhead and enables real-time robotic control.
significance: This breakthrough demonstrates that high-frequency VLA inference is achievable on consumer GPUs, opening the door to real-world autonomous systems.

title: Do You Really Need to Pretrain Q-Functions for Online RL Fine-Tuning?
headline: Do You Need to Pretrain Q-Functions for Online RL Fine-Tuning?
tldr: This study challenges the convention that Q-functions must be pretrained before online fine-tuning. It shows that starting with a randomly initialized Q-function can yield comparable or better performance, questioning the necessity of offline pretraining for value-based RL.
significance: The findings simplify RL pipelines by potentially eliminating a costly pretraining step, accelerating deployment of online RL agents.

title: Anomalies in Hadronic $B \to VV$ Decays
headline: New 4.1σ Discrepancy in Charmless B→VV Decays Challenges SU(3) Symmetry
tldr: A recent fit of charmless B→VV decays shows a 4.1σ deviation from the Standard Model prediction under SU(3) symmetry. This suggests potential new physics or the need to revisit flavor symmetry assumptions.
significance: The result highlights a significant tension that could point to physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: Mental World Modeling
headline: Integrating Mental State into World Models for Predictive Human Behavior
tldr: World models currently predict physical evolution but ignore agents' hidden mental states. Incorporating beliefs, desires, and intentions can improve planning and action in dynamic environments.
significance: Understanding and modeling human mental states is essential for accurate predictions and effective AI-driven decision making.

title: Mixed partition functions are exactly the graph parameters of exponentially bounded edge-connection rank
headline: Mixed Partition Functions Characterize Exponentially Bounded Edge-Connection Rank in Graph Parameters
tldr: The paper proves that a graph parameter with f(∅)=1 has exponentially bounded edge-connection rank if and only if it is a mixed partition function, and explicitly bounds the numbers of even and odd colours in the model. This resolves a conjecture of Regts and Sevenster by constructing a connection category and a rigid symmetric C‑category from f.
significance: It settles a key conjecture linking combinatorial rank constraints to partition function representations, advancing the theory of graph parameters.

title: From Classification to Regression: Using a Fruitfly to Solve Equations
headline: Fruitfly-Inspired Classification Approach Enables Efficient Nonlinear Regression Without Complex Global Models
tldr: We propose a novel regression framework that transforms nonlinear input-output relationships into a classification problem, inspired by fruitfly sensory mechanisms. By using a finite library of local patterns instead of global surrogate models, the method achieves efficient and scalable learning on limited scientific data.
significance: This approach offers a scalable alternative to traditional surrogate modeling, improving regression performance on sparse datasets.

title: VidMap: Exploiting Temporal Structure for Video-Based Structure-from-Motion
headline: VidMap: Leveraging Temporal Structure to Unlock Accurate Video-Based 3D Reconstruction
tldr: VidMap introduces a novel approach to recover camera calibration and metric poses from unconstrained videos by exploiting temporal structure, overcoming limitations of traditional SLAM. The method achieves accurate, globally consistent 3D reconstructions, enabling large-scale training data for navigation and scene understanding.
significance: By providing robust, globally consistent pose estimation from arbitrary videos, VidMap paves the way for scalable, high-fidelity datasets for autonomous navigation and scene understanding.

title: Non-Minimally Coupled Chain Inflation at High Scales
headline: Non-Minimally Coupled Chain Inflation: High-Scale Dynamics, Quantum Tunneling, and Early Universe Expansion
tldr: Chain inflation posits that the early Universe underwent a series of rapid quantum tunneling events between metastable vacua, providing an alternative to slow-roll inflation. At high energy scales, scalar fields naturally couple non‑minimally to gravity, influencing the tunneling dynamics and the resulting cosmological evolution.
significance: This framework offers a testable mechanism for generating the observed cosmic microwave background fluctuations while addressing the hierarchy of vacuum transitions in the early Universe.

title: The Fidelity and Feedback Traps: The Case for Health Digital Twins as Modular Evolving Causal Systems
headline: Health Digital Twins: Avoiding Fidelity and Feedback Traps in Modular Causal Modeling
tldr: Digital twins in healthcare can compare treatments and project patient trajectories, but copying engineering twin designs can lead to fidelity and feedback traps. The paper argues for modular, evolving causal systems that better capture the complexity of biological data.
significance: This work highlights critical pitfalls in applying mechanical digital twin frameworks to health, guiding more realistic and effective modeling strategies.

title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
headline: Can AI Agents Automate Open-Ended AI Research? Early Case Study Evidence
tldr: This study examines whether autonomous AI agents can conduct open-ended AI research, using two case studies. It highlights the limitations of current evaluation methods and proposes a new framework for assessing agent-driven research.
significance: The findings suggest that while AI agents show promise, robust evaluation frameworks are essential for reliable progress.

title: APEX-Accounting
headline: APEX-Accounting: A New Benchmark for Evaluating AI Models on Real-World Accounting Tasks
tldr: APEX-Accounting, developed by Mercor and Ramp, tests whether large language models can perform core accounting functions such as reconciliation, expense accrual, transaction posting, and report generation. The benchmark includes 160 tasks across 10 worlds featuring diverse data formats like spreadsheets, PDFs, and more.
significance: This benchmark pushes the limits of foundation models in automating complex, real-world financial workflows, offering a rigorous standard for future AI accounting solutions.

title: The evolution of galaxy dust scaling relations in the COLIBRE simulations
headline: Tracing Dust Evolution Across Cosmic Time in COLIBRE Simulations
tldr: We map dust mass functions from z=15 to z=0 using the COLIBRE simulations, capturing dust production, growth, and destruction in a multiphase ISM. The results reveal evolving dust scaling relations that match observations and provide benchmarks for future models.
significance: These findings offer a comprehensive, self-consistent framework for dust evolution that can calibrate galaxy formation models and interpret observational data across epochs.

title: Pass the Baton: Trajectory-Relayed On-Policy Distillation
headline: Mitigating Prefix Failure in On-Policy Distillation with Trajectory Relays for Large Language Models
tldr: On-policy distillation uses the student’s own trajectory for supervision but suffers from prefix failure, where early mistakes lead to cascading errors. This paper introduces a trajectory-relayed approach that passes supervision only after correct prefixes, reducing misdirected continuations and saving compute.
significance: This work offers a principled solution to prefix failure in on-policy distillation, enabling more reliable and efficient training of large language models.

title: $π\mathbf{R}^2$: Reactive Real-time Flow Policies
headline: Bridging the Gap: Real-Time Reactive Flow Policies for Generalist Manipulation
tldr: Action-chunking flow policies built on large backbones run open-loop, losing reactivity. Frequent replanning could restore responsiveness, but the perception-to-action pipeline is too slow, limiting real-time performance.
significance: This work highlights the trade-off between computational efficiency and reactivity in large-scale manipulation policies, pointing toward faster perception pipelines.

title: Proportional Fairness for Harmful Decisions
headline: Revisiting Core Concepts for Allocating Public Bads: Proportional Fairness Approach
tldr: We analyze the allocation of public bads and show that traditional core definitions fail. We propose new formal criteria for proportional fairness in this context.
significance: This work reshapes fairness criteria for public bad allocation, guiding policy design.

title: Spend Experts Where You Are Unsure: Confidence-Adaptive Routing for Mixture-of-Experts LoRA
headline: Confidence-Adaptive Routing Boosts Mixture-of-Experts LoRA Efficiency
tldr: Mixture-of-Experts LoRA traditionally routes each token to a fixed number of experts, which can waste capacity on easy tokens and under-serve hard ones. By interpreting the router’s output distribution as a per-token uncertainty signal, the authors propose a confidence-adaptive routing scheme that dynamically adjusts the number of experts per token, improving efficiency and performance.
significance: This approach optimizes resource allocation in large language models, reducing computational cost while maintaining or improving accuracy.

title: QuickGWecc: Fast Bayesian pipeline for searching eccentric binaries in pulsar timing array data
headline: Fast Bayesian Pipeline Uncovers Eccentric SMBH Binaries in Pulsar Timing Data
tldr: QuickGWecc introduces a rapid Bayesian framework for detecting eccentric supermassive black hole binaries in pulsar timing array data. It significantly reduces computational cost while maintaining sensitivity, paving the way for timely identification of continuous gravitational waves.
significance: This method accelerates the search for individual gravitational wave sources, enabling quicker multimessenger follow-up.

title: S2A2: Audio-Visual Imitation Learning for Manipulation Tasks Using Acoustic Spatial Information
headline: Robots Learn to Manipulate Using Sound: Acoustic Imitation for Object Localization
tldr: This paper introduces acoustic-aware manipulation tasks where robots use auditory cues to locate and manipulate objects, requiring sound source localization and active exploration. It demonstrates that integrating acoustic spatial information improves imitation learning for manipulation.
significance: It shows that auditory cues can be leveraged for real-time robotic manipulation, expanding the sensory modalities for imitation learning.

title: Photonuclear Neutron Production in OpenMC: Verification Against MCNPX, FLUKA, and a First-Collision Analytical Solution
headline: Verifying Photonuclear Neutron Production in OpenMC with MCNPX, FLUKA, and Analytics
tldr: OpenMC’s photonuclear module was benchmarked against MCNPX, FLUKA, and an analytical model. The results confirm its accuracy for high-energy photon-induced neutron production.
significance: This validation establishes OpenMC as a reliable tool for simulating photonuclear reactions in diverse high-energy applications.

title: Re-thinking Mammography Transfer Learning: The Dataset-Informed Transfer Learning (DITL) Framework for Breast Cancer Screening and Lesion Diagnosis
headline: Dataset-Informed Transfer Learning Boosts Mammography Classification Accuracy
tldr: The DITL framework tailors transfer learning to the specific characteristics of each mammography dataset, outperforming conventional methods. It demonstrates improved diagnostic performance on both small curated sets and large clinical cohorts.
significance: This approach addresses a key limitation in medical imaging AI by enabling scalable, dataset-aware transfer learning, potentially improving breast cancer screening outcomes.

title: VetClaw: An Edge-Cloud Multimodal Agentic System for Veterinary Disease Screening
headline: VetClaw: Edge-Cloud Multimodal System for Rapid Veterinary Disease Screening Using Vision-Language Models
tldr: VetClaw combines an edge camera and a cloud-hosted vision‑language model to perform zero‑shot disease classification from images and optional text. The system decouples agent interaction from workflow orchestration, enabling real‑time veterinary screening in remote settings.
significance: VetClaw demonstrates how multimodal foundation models can be deployed in edge‑cloud pipelines to provide timely, accurate disease screening for veterinary practitioners worldwide.

title: Data Pyramid for Embodied Manipulation
headline: A Structured Data Pyramid for Training Embodied Manipulation Agents Across Domains
tldr: The paper proposes a five-layer data pyramid that integrates real, simulated, synthetic, annotated, and multimodal sources to bridge the observation-action gap in embodied manipulation. It demonstrates how combining these layers can scale training of foundation models for physical interaction tasks.
significance: This framework unifies diverse data modalities, enabling scalable training of embodied agents and accelerating progress in robotics and AI.

title: ClinFusion: A Vision-Centric Multimodal LLM System for Holistic Medical Understanding
headline: ClinFusion: Vision-Centric Multimodal LLM Revolutionizing Holistic Medical Image Understanding Across Modalities
tldr: ClinFusion integrates 2D and 3D medical images into a multimodal large language model, enabling fine‑grained, factual assessments aligned with radiologists' workflows. The system introduces new evaluation protocols that mirror clinical practice and demonstrates improved diagnostic accuracy.
significance: ClinFusion bridges the gap between vision‑based medical data and language models, offering a scalable, clinically relevant tool for radiology.

title: Measuring Cosmic Neutrino Masses Independently of Dark Energy
headline: New Constraints on Cosmic Neutrino Masses Independent of Dark Energy
tldr: Neutrino oscillations confirm mass, but cosmological limits depend on dark energy assumptions. This study derives robust neutrino mass bounds using CMB, BAO, and lensing data independent of dark energy, tightening the sum of masses to <0.12 eV.
significance: It provides a model‑independent upper limit on neutrino mass, crucial for particle physics and cosmology.

title: Certified Parallel-in-Time Sinkhorn for Dynamic Entropic Optimal Transport
headline: Parallel-in-Time Sinkhorn Accelerates Dynamic Entropic Optimal Transport for Real-Time Applications
tldr: We introduce TemporalSinkhorn, a parallel-in-time algorithm that batches future candidates and repairs, eliminating sequential bottlenecks in entropic optimal transport. This approach enables faster, accurate solutions for dynamic flow matching without sacrificing output fidelity.
significance: TemporalSinkhorn dramatically reduces computation time for dynamic optimal transport, enabling real-time deployment in time-series applications.

title: Demonstrating the integration of a photonic lantern with an all-fiber-based nulling interferometer
headline: Integrating Photonic Lanterns into All-Fiber Nulling Interferometers for Exoplanet Imaging
tldr: A new approach couples photonic lanterns with fiber-based nulling interferometers, enabling deeper starlight suppression at smaller angular separations. This technique promises higher contrast imaging of exoplanets and protoplanets at Solar System scales.
significance: It advances high-contrast imaging, pushing the limits of exoplanet detection closer to host stars.

title: Gravitational waves from super-Hubble bubbles
headline: Super-Hubble Bubble Collisions: New Gravitational Wave Signatures from Inflationary Phase Transitions
tldr: During inflation, true‑vacuum bubbles can nucleate but only collide after inflation ends, producing bubbles larger than the Hubble radius. These super‑Hubble collisions generate distinctive gravitational‑wave spectra that could be detectable by future observatories.
significance: This mechanism offers a novel source of primordial gravitational waves that could probe physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: Atmospheric Escape Rates of Planets in Stellar Tidal Fields from 3-D Hydrodynamic Simulations1
headline: 3‑D Simulations Reveal How Stellar Tides Shape Atmospheric Escape in Close‑In Planets
tldr: Using full 3‑D hydrodynamic models, we quantify how stellar tidal forces influence photo‑evaporation and core‑powered mass loss in a Jupiter‑sized planet. The results show that tidal fields can significantly enhance escape rates, reshaping the planet’s atmospheric evolution.
significance: This study provides the first comprehensive 3‑D benchmark for atmospheric escape under tidal effects, improving predictions for exoplanet demographics.

title: Learning Distributions from Multiple Data Providers
headline: Learning Distributions from Multiple Data Providers: A Conditional Sampling Approach
tldr: We study a stylized model for learning an unknown distribution on a finite domain using restricted conditional samples from a fixed family of queryable sets. The framework captures learning from heterogeneous, overlapping data providers and yields sample complexity bounds that depend on the structure of the query sets.
significance: This work provides a theoretical foundation for efficient distribution learning in settings where data is fragmented across multiple sources, informing future designs of data integration systems.

title: Rethinking Classifier-Free Guidance in On-Policy Diffusion Distillation
headline: Revisiting Classifier-Free Guidance for On-Policy Diffusion Distillation in Modern Systems
tldr: This paper investigates how classifier-free guidance (CFG) interacts with on-policy diffusion distillation (OPD). It proposes a new approach that aligns teacher and student guided predictions, improving performance on diffusion tasks.
significance: It bridges a gap in understanding CFG's role in OPD, enabling more efficient diffusion model training.

title: KANEx: Translating Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks' Interpretability to Medical Explainability
headline: KANEx: Bridging Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks to Explainable Chest X-ray AI for Clinicians
tldr: KANEx adapts Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks to provide transparent, visual explanations for chest X-ray classifiers, complementing Vision‑Language Models with interpretable visual cues. This approach restores clinician trust by revealing the decision logic behind AI predictions.
significance: By marrying mathematical interpretability with medical AI, KANEx offers a practical path to trustworthy diagnostic tools.

title: Classical simulation and model concentration in passive linear optics
headline: Exploring Classical Simulability and Barren Plateaus in Passive Linear Optics for Bosonic Systems
tldr: Passive linear optics offers quantum advantage for sampling tasks but its classical simulability remains unclear. Researchers investigate whether barren plateaus, known to hinder qubit models, also affect bosonic systems.
significance: Understanding this tradeoff could determine the practicality of near‑term bosonic quantum algorithms.

title: Infrared Imaging Empowered by Artificial Intelligence for Pediatric Skeletal Triage: A Narrative Review and Future Perspectives
headline: AI-Enhanced Infrared Imaging for Rapid Pediatric Skeletal Triage
tldr: This review examines how infrared imaging combined with deep learning can provide a radiation-free alternative for pediatric skeletal triage. It highlights current evidence, challenges, and future directions for integrating AI-powered IR diagnostics into emergency care.
significance: AI-driven infrared imaging offers a promising, low-risk triage tool that could reduce cumulative radiation exposure in children.

title: Robot-Factored World Models via Robot Rendering
headline: Robot-Factored World Models: Rendering Actions for Accurate Future Observation Prediction
tldr: We propose a robot-factored world model that separates robot motion from scene dynamics, improving action-conditioned video predictions. By rendering robot actions explicitly, the model better captures contact and object motion, leading to more accurate future observation forecasts.
significance: This approach enhances predictive accuracy in robotics by decoupling robot control from environmental response, enabling more reliable planning.

title: SM4RT: Learning Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction
headline: SM4RT: Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction with Foundation Models
tldr: SM4RT introduces a novel approach that learns structured motion geometry, enabling accurate 4D reconstruction from monocular imagery. By leveraging geometry foundation models, it overcomes the limitations of point‑wise motion methods and captures coherent physical motion.
significance: This work advances dynamic 3D reconstruction by integrating structured motion modeling into foundation models, paving the way for more realistic and scalable 4D scene understanding.

title: Twins: Learn to Predict Unified Representations with Focal Loss
headline: Twins: Predict Unified Visual Representations Using Focal Loss for Multimodal Models
tldr: The Twins framework learns a shared visual token space that bridges semantic and generative representations by predicting unified embeddings with a focal loss. This approach resolves mismatched latent spaces in continuous pipelines, improving both multimodal understanding and image synthesis.
significance: By aligning semantic and generative latent spaces, Twins enhances the compatibility of foundation models for downstream vision tasks and generative applications.

title: ViTacWorld: Scaling Visuo-Tactile World Models for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
headline: ViTacWorld: Scaling Visuo‑Tactile Models Using Action‑Conditioned Learning for Robust Contact‑Rich Robot Manipulation
tldr: ViTacWorld introduces an action‑conditioned visuo‑tactile world model that learns from limited real‑world tactile data, enabling robots to perform contact‑rich manipulation tasks with higher robustness. The framework leverages a scalable dataset and open‑source architecture, demonstrating state‑of‑the‑art performance across diverse manipulation scenarios.
significance: By bridging the gap between visual perception and tactile sensing, ViTacWorld paves the way for more reliable and generalizable robot manipulation in real‑world settings.

title: Skill Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of LLM Capability with Co-Evolving Skills
headline: Skill Self-Play: Advancing LLMs via Co-Evolving Skills and Self-Generated Tasks
tldr: LLMs are moving from manual annotation to interaction-driven self-evolution. Current methods struggle to balance narrow, verifiable tasks with broad, open-ended generation.
significance: This work proposes a framework that reconciles task diversity with reliable verification, enabling LLMs to autonomously expand their skill set.

title: Effective field theories of nonlinear fluctuating hydrodynamics in one dimension
headline: Effective Field Theories Illuminate Superdiffusive Transport in One-Dimensional Nonlinear Hydrodynamics
tldr: This work develops effective field theories to capture the emergent superdiffusive transport observed in one-dimensional interacting systems. By integrating nonlinear fluctuating hydrodynamics, it provides a framework that bypasses perturbative limitations inherent to low-dimensional physics.
significance: It offers a powerful theoretical tool to predict and analyze anomalous transport phenomena that defy conventional diffusion models.

title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers
headline: Explainable Reinforcement Learning Enhances Trust and Decision-Making for Air Traffic Controllers
tldr: This study demonstrates how explainable reinforcement learning can support air traffic controllers by providing transparent, real-time decision guidance. The approach improves trust and safety in high-stakes aviation operations.
significance: By making AI decisions interpretable, the research paves the way for safer, more reliable automation in air traffic management.

title: Machine-Checked Arithmetic Bit Complexity of the Kannan-Bachem Smith Normal Form in Lean 4
headline: Formal Verification of Smith Normal Form Algorithm in Lean 4 with Bit Complexity Analysis
tldr: We formalize the Kannan–Bachem Smith normal form algorithm for integer matrices in Lean 4, proving correctness and inverse identities. Additionally, we analyze and bound the bit complexity, showing termination via decreasing binary size.
significance: This work provides the first machine-checked proof of the Smith normal form algorithm’s correctness and complexity, enhancing trust in formalized algebraic tools.

title: Gridnberg: A Topography-Aware Pedestrian Routing Dataset for New York City
headline: Gridnberg: Topography-Aware Pedestrian Routing Dataset for New York City Streets
tldr: This paper presents Gridnberg, a dataset that incorporates elevation data into pedestrian routing for NYC, addressing limitations of planar street graphs. The dataset improves route impedance modeling and accessibility analysis by accounting for grade differences across the city.
significance: Gridnberg enables more accurate pedestrian navigation and urban planning by integrating topography into street network analysis.

title: The Regression Tax: Decomposing Why Skills Help and Hurt LLM Agents
headline: When Adding Skills to LLMs Backfires: The Regression Tax Explained
tldr: Adding procedural skills to LLM agents can improve or degrade performance. Our large-scale study across 6,000 runs shows that the average success metric masks a hidden regression cost, guiding better skill integration.
significance: This work uncovers a critical trade-off in LLM agent design, showing that skill augmentation can backfire and must be carefully evaluated.

title: PinEqualizer: Full Funnel Content Exploration and Debiasing System at Pinterest
headline: PinEqualizer: Debiasing Cold-Start Content Across Pinterest's Search and Recommendation Funnel
tldr: PinEqualizer tackles the content cold-start problem by exploring new content throughout the entire multi-stage funnel. It generalizes to both search and recommendation surfaces while reducing bias toward existing content.
significance: It enables fairer, more diverse content exposure at scale, improving user engagement.

title: Is S301 the Captured Companion of the Hypervelocity Star S5-HVS1?
headline: S301 Reveals Captured Companion of Hypervelocity Star S5-HVS1
tldr: The hypervelocity star S5-HVS1, ejected from the Galactic Center, implies a bound companion orbiting the supermassive black hole. GRAVITY observations of S301 confirm this companion, providing a direct test of the Hills mechanism.
significance: This discovery offers the first observational evidence linking a hypervelocity star to its captured counterpart, validating theoretical models of binary disruption near supermassive black holes.

title: On the strong coupling limit of Yang-Mills matrix models
headline: Strong Coupling in Mass‑Deformed Yang–Mills Matrix Models
tldr: We study the strong coupling limit of mass‑deformed Yang–Mills matrix models and find that quantum fluctuations can prevent the matrices from becoming effectively commuting, challenging the emergence of a classical space interpretation.
significance: This analysis clarifies when non‑commutative geometry arises in matrix models, informing approaches to quantum gravity.

title: A geometric framework for spin relaxation
headline: Unified Geometric Framework Unveils Spin Relaxation Dynamics via Covariant Relaxation Tensor
tldr: The study introduces a covariant relaxation tensor in Liouville space that unifies longitudinal and transverse spin relaxation rates. By projecting this tensor, conventional R1 and R2 rates emerge, revealing deeper structural unity.
significance: This framework simplifies spin relaxation analysis, potentially impacting quantum computing and magnetic resonance research.

title: Where You Tap Matters: A Probe-and-Model Benchmark for Open-Set RF Fingerprinting
headline: Where to Tap: Benchmarking Open-Set RF Fingerprinting in Receiver Chains
tldr: The paper introduces a probe-and-model benchmark that evaluates optimal sampling points in the receiver chain for RF fingerprinting, addressing inconsistencies in prior studies. It offers a standardized dataset and evaluation protocol for open-set transmitter identification, promoting reproducible research.
significance: This benchmark clarifies optimal sampling points for RF fingerprinting, enabling more accurate and reproducible transmitter identification across diverse receiver designs.

title: Fault-tolerant quantum algorithms for simulating atomic nuclei
headline: Fault-Tolerant Quantum Algorithms Enable Accurate Simulation of Atomic Nuclei for Nuclear Physics
tldr: We develop and compile fault-tolerant quantum algorithms that simulate the structure of atomic nuclei, a domain largely unexplored by quantum computing. These algorithms pave the way for precise nuclear physics studies on future quantum hardware.
significance: This work extends quantum computing’s reach into nuclear physics, offering a new tool for probing fundamental interactions in atomic nuclei.

title: Graph Learning on Ensembles of Cyclic Peptides: An Investigation of Molecular Ensemble Modeling
headline: EnsembleEGNN: Learning Molecular Ensembles of Cyclic Peptides for Property Prediction
tldr: We present EnsembleEGNN, a foundation model that encodes each conformer of cyclic peptides with shared EGNN layers and pools the representations to predict molecular properties. This approach captures conformational diversity and outperforms single-conformer baselines.
significance: By modeling entire conformational ensembles, EnsembleEGNN improves the accuracy of property predictions for flexible molecules, advancing drug discovery.

title: Identifying and Distinguishing Quenching Galaxies with Spatially Resolved Star Formation in the Hubble Frontier Fields
headline: Mapping Quenching Signatures in Hubble Frontier Fields Galaxies with Spatially Resolved Star Formation
tldr: We analyze 1,437 galaxies in the Hubble Frontier Fields, using spatially resolved SED fitting to identify quenching patterns. Our results reveal distinct quenching mechanisms and their spatial distribution, enhancing our understanding of galaxy evolution.
significance: This study provides the first comprehensive spatially resolved view of quenching across a large sample of distant galaxies, informing models of galaxy evolution.

title: Unsupervised Consensus-Based Anomaly Detection for Spatiotemporal Malaria Incidence in Ghana
headline: Mapping Malaria Anomalies in Ghana: Unsupervised Consensus Detection Reveals Hotspots
tldr: A consensus-based framework identified spatiotemporal anomalies in Ghana’s malaria data, highlighting persistent hotspots in Ashanti, Northern, and Greater Accra regions. The study underscores the importance of spatially explicit surveillance for targeted interventions.
significance: The findings provide actionable insights for malaria control by pinpointing recurrent anomaly hotspots, enabling focused resource allocation.

title: Beyond Sycophancy: Structured Resistance and Compliance in LLM Moral Reasoning
headline: LLMs Must Balance Sycophancy and Moral Judgment: Structured Resistance and Compliance
tldr: This study explores how large language models can learn from others while avoiding sycophancy, by distinguishing when to incorporate external perspectives and when to uphold their own moral judgments. The authors analyze the resistance-compliance dynamics across three scenarios, offering insights for building socially calibrated LLMs.
significance: Understanding resistance-compliance in LLMs is crucial for developing AI that can engage ethically with diverse viewpoints without compromising its own moral integrity.

title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
headline: OpenForgeRL Enables End-to-End Training of Harness-Native AI Agents Across Environments
tldr: OpenForgeRL provides a framework that integrates complex inference harnesses like Claude Code and Codex into open-source RL training pipelines, allowing end-to-end learning of stateful, multi-process agents. This approach removes the need for proprietary infrastructure and expands the applicability of advanced AI agents to any environment.
significance: It democratizes advanced AI agent training by making harness-native capabilities accessible within open-source reinforcement learning stacks.

title: Visual Contrastive Self-Distillation
headline: Combining Visual Evidence and Privileged Answers for On-Policy Self-Distillation
tldr: On-policy self-distillation eliminates external teachers but still requires asymmetric signals. This work investigates merging visual evidence and privileged answers to strengthen the self-teacher’s guidance.
significance: It offers a more robust self-distillation framework that could improve policy learning without external supervision.

title: SANA-Video 2.0: Hybrid Linear Attention with Attention Residuals for Efficient Video Generation
headline: SANA-Video 2.0: Hybrid Linear Attention Boosts Video Diffusion to 720p on One GPU
tldr: SANA-Video 2.0 introduces a hybrid linear‑softmax attention mechanism that enables 5B and 14B video diffusion transformers to generate 720p video on a single GPU while matching full‑softmax quality. The architecture preserves long‑sequence scaling and eliminates quadratic attention costs, making high‑resolution video generation more efficient.
significance: This work demonstrates that hybrid attention can bring large‑scale video diffusion models to practical hardware without sacrificing quality, paving the way for real‑time high‑resolution video synthesis.

title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
headline: MIRROR: Enhancing Vision-Language Models by Leveraging Alternate Viewpoints for Better Reasoning
tldr: The paper introduces MIRROR, a method that trains vision-language models to learn from complementary text and diagram views, improving performance on geometry reasoning tasks. It demonstrates that models can transfer knowledge between modalities, closing the gap with large language models.
significance: MIRROR shows that cross-view training can substantially boost visual reasoning in VLMs, providing a new direction for multimodal AI.

title: Seeking Help in the Digital Age: A Cross-Platform Analysis of Online Support Systems for Technology-Facilitated Abuse Victims
headline: Cross-Platform Analysis of Online Support for Technology-Facilitated Abuse Victims
tldr: This study evaluates how digital platforms provide guidance to victims of technology-facilitated abuse, examining the effectiveness of web, mobile, and social media channels. Findings reveal disparities in resource quality and highlight best practices for safer online support.
significance: It informs policy makers and developers on improving digital safety resources for abuse victims.

title: The Frankl--Tokushige product conjectures for $r$-cross-intersecting families
headline: Sharp Inequality for r-Cross-Intersecting Families Solves Frankl–Tokushige Product Conjecture Uniformly
tldr: We prove a sharp product inequality for r-cross-intersecting families, confirming both the uniform and biased Frankl–Tokushige conjectures. The bound matches the natural extremal families and is achieved by level sets of the Boolean lattice.
significance: This resolves a long-standing open problem in extremal set theory, establishing optimal bounds for intersecting families across multiple parameters.
